cells.tense: You are standing in the middle of your own direction, and it is holding.
cells.ask: Tell one person who is in it with you what you are keeping steady and why it still matters — today, out loud, without asking them to agree.
cells.core:
You feel with people and you do not lose your line. That is what is running now. The people around you can push and want and differ, and your sense of what matters stays standing — because it came from what you actually care about, not from what you are defending against.

Something quiet is doing work underneath. It is what lets someone bring you a hard thing and leave intact, and it is why time with you carries a little more. Feed it: say out loud to one person what you are keeping steady and why, while there is nothing to defend it from. What is kept also wants to be told.
cells.sheetLine: You keep your direction while staying open to people.
cells.verb: gathering what has scattered into one steady point and holding it there
cells.place: the place where two people meet as they really are, difference intact

cells.tense: You are already living past a resistance that has not arrived yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are defending right now and stop defending it for a day — let the outcome happen unguarded and notice you are still here.
cells.core:
You love people and you are bracing for a fight. Your reading of someone's mood, your half-formed answers, your preparation for what might happen between you — all of it is set somewhere ahead, guarding. The people in front of you are getting the defense, not the person.

The effort is real and the spending is early. What you are rehearsing has not been earned by anything that is actually here. So choose one thing you are defending, put it down for a day, and let it go unguarded. Not to win or lose — to find out whether the weight was yours to carry. What holds without your arms up holds better.

cells.tense: You are still behind a door that closed, and it is not open now.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about where you are right now to one person who gets it — not about what you are keeping steady, about who you are.
cells.core:
The direction is still yours, but the room you got it in is gone. Since then you have let yourself be visible less — less of what matters to you, less of what has changed. That is not coldness. It is the distance of someone who got most of the way out and stopped at the frame.

What has gone unsaid is what you have wanted from being seen as yourself. Choose one person who can hold it and say where you actually are — what you want, not what the situation requires. The showing is asking them to meet you, not dragging them into anything. Keep it small and inside the day.

cells.tense: You are already keeping a direction steady and calling it nothing you did.
cells.ask: Say to one person, in your own words, that the direction you have been keeping steady is yours — then keep at it as a choice, not a condition.
cells.core:
You already steady yourself around the people who matter to you. When someone needs contact and you pick it up without being told, when you gate your own plans so another person's day works, when you stay warm across disagreement — that is your direction in motion, and those mornings were not spent guarding something you did not choose.

The work is real. The name on it is missing. The steadying shows up as just how you are or what the week is asking, so the one person who could claim it holds back. Say out loud to one person that this direction is yours. Then keep at it, but on purpose.
